items.title: 'I should've been the one to resign,' says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP Deputy National Publicity Secretary Hannah Yeoh has expressed regret over Anthony Loke's decision to resign as Transport Minister with immediate effect today. Earlier, Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, announced that his resignation as Transport minister would take effect immediately. Media reports had previously said Loke had submitted his resignation letter as Transport minister to the prime minister on Sept 28.

items.title: ‘Alhamdulillah’: Rosmah welcomes news of Najib’s clearance for house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has expressed gratitude following the return of her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to their residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here today after a court order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house detention. She said she was awaiting Najib’s arrival at their Taman Duta home, where he will serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house detention. Earlier today, the High Court issued a fresh order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his reduced six-year prison term under house detention until Aug 23, 2028, with immediate effect.

items.title: Investigation papers on Penang assemblyman accused of injuring wife still under DPP review
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — Penang police are awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) on the investigation into an allegation that a state assemblyman injured his wife in an incident on October 31. Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the investigation papers were still with the DPP's office for further review. "The investigation papers are still with the DPP, and police are awaiting further instructions on the case," he told Bernama when contacted tonight for an update on the investigation.

items.title: Expired import permit leads to seizure of 25 tonnes of frozen chicken
items.summary: BUKIT KAYU HITAM: Nearly 25 tonnes of frozen chicken worth RM562,290 were seized by the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) after the importer was found to have submitted an expired import permit. The seizure followed a physical inspection by MCBA officers at the Bilik Sejuk Beli, Block E1, Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex, yesterday. The inspection found that the frozen chicken products, categorised as 'Chicken Thigh & Leg Boneless Frozen', had been imported from Thailand.

items.title: Vehicles believed to be carrying Najib's family arrive at Langgak Duta home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Several vehicles believed to be carrying family members of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrived at his residence in Langgak Duta here tonight. The vehicles arrived at 7.55pm. Earlier, a Prisons Department vehicle arrived at the residence around 7pm.

items.title: Advancecon bags RM41.5mil Johor job
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Advancecon Holdings Bhd has secured a RM41.52 million contract for earthworks and infrastructure works at Southern Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) in Kulai, Johor. The project, undertaken by subsidiary Advancecon Infra Sdn Bhd, is expected to take 19 months to complete. Advancecon said the development is expected to contribute to strengthening Johor's position as a regional investment destination.

items.title: Home Ministry ready to implement Najib's house arrest order
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Home Ministry is ready to implement the High Court's decision ordering former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028. "The High Court today ordered that the Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine dated Nov 6 be set aside and replaced with a Conditional Pardon Order, requiring the accused to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence under house arrest at No. "The High Court's decision today has clarified these questions," he said.

items.title: Jati Tinggi unit wins RM33.09mil data centre power infrastructure works
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Jati Tinggi Group Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary, Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd, has secured a RM33.09 million contract for power infrastructure works to support a data centre in Gerbil, Negeri Sembilan. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, it said the contract involves the supply, design, installation, testing and commissioning of two circuits of 275 kilovolt power cables connecting the transition yard to the data centre substation. It also covers the construction of a transition yard, overhead line T-off works and related secondary system modifications to support the data centre's interim power supply infrastructure requirements.

items.title: Sunway REIT's Q3 net profit falls to RM116.17mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit) today reported a lower net profit of RM116.17 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) compared to RM121.85 a year earlier. Revenue, however, grew to RM675.67 million from RM666.69 million previously, driven by a stronger contribution of RM43.1 million from the retail segment, more than offsetting the absence of RM29.3 million in revenue contribution from Sunway university and college campus. Sunway Reit Management chief executive officer Derek Teh Wan Wei said Sunway Reit continued to demonstrate the resilience and quality of its diversified portfolio in Q3 2026.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against US dollar amid hopes of de-escalation in US-Iran conflict
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended marginally higher against the US dollar on Tuesday, supported by improving market sentiment amid expectations of a de-escalation of the US-Iran conflict. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said this came as US President Donald Trump indicated that further strikes against Iran were unnecessary. "The ringgit traded mostly within a narrow range against the US dollar today, fluctuating between RM4.0510 and RM4.0590.

items.title: Home Ministry says ready to carry out Najib’s house arrest; court order today cleared the air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Home Ministry this evening said it is prepared to carry out a new court order today for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to be on house arrest until August 2028. In his statement on his ministry’s readiness to execute the court’s new order, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the High Court’s latest order has helped answered legal uncertainties surrounding Najib’s house arrest. He was referring to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur’s decision this afternoon to revoke an earlier November 6 “Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine” and to replace it with a new order that will require Najib to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028.

items.title: Zahid: BN can do better than Anwar-led government
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says the coalition can deliver an even better government than the current administration led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, which he acknowledged had performed well and achieved much. Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, was speaking at a gathering with Melaka Community Development Department (Kemas) personnel. Also present were Rural and Regional Development Ministry deputy secretary-general (policy) Datuk Abdul Kahar Abdullah, Melaka senior executive councillor Datuk Rais Yasin and Kemas director-general Datuk Mohd Hanafiah Man.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest: What did the AGC ask the High Court to clarify today?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today sought to ensure that Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest arrangements explicitly provided for his return to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve his separate 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) prison sentence. In its written application, the prosecution requested that the High Court replace a November 6 discharge order with new terms clarifying Najib’s remaining SRC International sentence and his subsequent imprisonment in the 1MDB case. It also sought to specify that his SRC sentence would end on August 23, 2028, with his return to prison subject to any court order then in force.

items.title: Zahid expresses gratitude over court ruling on Najib's house arrest
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has expressed gratitude following the High Court's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest with immediate effect. "We also wish to express our deepest gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who chaired the Pardons Board and decided that Najib could serve the remainder of his sentence at home. Zahid hoped the latest development would put an end to the prolonged controversy surrounding the implementation of the royal addendum order allowing Najib to serve his sentence under house arrest.

items.title: Penang cops told to step up preparations for monsoon disasters
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Police departments and district headquarters across Penang have been ordered to strengthen logistical and operational preparations ahead of anticipated disasters during the northeast monsoon. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said personnel deployment, operational assets and coordination with other agencies must be stepped up immediately to ensure swift responses. "All departments and districts must reinforce preparations in terms of personnel deployment, operational assets and coordination with relevant agencies.

items.title: Zahid wishes Loke 'all the best'
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has described Anthony Loke as a principled leader who stands by his convictions. Commenting on the DAP secretary-general's resignation as transport minister, Zahid said he respected the Seremban member of Parliament's decision and appreciated his service and cooperation as a cabinet member. Zahid said Loke's departure would be felt by other cabinet members, particularly as he was a senior member of the unity government Cabinet.

items.title: How uncertainty over university pathways shapes Chinese youths’ choices
items.summary: In a research conducted by IMAN Research, they found that uncertainty over public university admissions, differences between pre-university pathways and concerns about access to certain courses had influenced how some the research participants approached their education. Some participants described choosing private education or overseas study rather than applying through the public university admission system. The report describes these decisions as examples of how young people may seek alternatives when public pathways appear uncertain.

items.title: Foreign buying lifts bond holdings by RM7.2bil to RM325.5bil
items.summary: The firm said the US Treasury (UST) yield curve experienced a flattening last month, averaging around 5.12 per cent on the back of heightened geopolitical risk and expectations for a delayed rate hike. In early October, a sharp sell-off temporarily pushed the 10-year UST yield to a multi-decade high of 5.342 per cent. The MGS 10-year yield traded between 3.799 per cent and 4.028 per cent last month, while the UST 10-year yield traded lower within the range of 4.930 per cent to 5.307 per cent.

items.title: Big Caring IPO final price at RM1.08, oversubscribed 4.31 times
items.summary: Malaysian Issuing House Sdn Bhd said the public portion, comprising 147.64 million shares, received 29,474 applications for 783.75 million shares. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd and RHB Investment Bank Bhd are the joint principal advisers, joint global coordinators, joint bookrunners, joint managing underwriters and joint underwriters for the IPO. AmInvestment Bank Bhd is also a joint principal adviser, joint global coordinator, joint bookrunner and joint underwriter.

items.title: Legal questions delayed Najib's house arrest implementation, says Saifuddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Legal questions over the interpretation of the conditional pardon order and a subsequent discharge order had delayed the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Responding to the High Court's decision today allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest, Saifuddin said the ruling had clarified the legal issues. He said questions surrounding the conditional pardon order and the Nov 6 discharge order, particularly the provision for house arrest, had held up its implementation.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 10, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed lower as selling pressure in energy and banking stocks weighed on the market. The key index dropped more than 12 points to 1,604. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin dropped to RM301,363.

items.title: Nepal flood victims' families may wait up to a year for death certificates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians missing in the Nepal floods could face another three to 12 months, or longer, to obtain certificates of presumption of death, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (Masfih) said. Its coordinator and spokesman, Dr R Manivannan, said the process could be prolonged by uncertainty over whether documents issued by Nepal would be recognised directly by Malaysia or require further legal procedures. He said it remained unclear whether families could submit the Nepali documents directly to the National Registration Department (NRD), or whether they would first need a court order or further assessment.

items.title: Rapid KL confirms brake fault behind smoke incident at KL Sentral (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Rapid KL today confirmed an incident involving one of its trains at KL Sentral station after smoke was seen coming from the train at about 5.15pm. In a statement, the rail operator said the incident is believed to have been caused by the train's braking system, which resulted in visible smoke being emitted from the affected train. Rapid KL said all passengers were safely disembarked at Bangsar station and were able to continue their journey on the next available train.

items.title: Najib arrives at Kajang Prison ahead of transfer to Taman Duta home
items.summary: KAJANG: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrived at Kajang Prison at 6.14pm for final preparations before being transferred to his residence to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. A convoy of five vehicles carrying Najib was seen entering the prison compound. Earlier, Najib's lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said Najib was expected to begin serving his sentence at home after stopping at Kajang Prison.

items.title: Najib posts 'Alhamdulillah' after court orders house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak has posted a brief "Alhamdulillah" message on his Facebook page following the High Court's order allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest. Najib's lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said Najib was expected to begin serving his sentence at home after stopping at Kajang Prison. Shafee said prison officers would read out the house arrest conditions to Najib at the prison before taking him to his Taman Duta residence.

items.title: Beyond assumptions: IMAN Research’s journey into the lives of Chinese youths
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — When Violet Lee Zi Yi began researching Malaysian Chinese youths, she admitted she initially approached the community with assumptions about its relative economic advantages, resources and access to opportunities. “I initially thought Chinese is a unitary block. It is so different,” Lee said in an interview about the findings of IMAN Research’s report, Kami Orang Sini Juga: Chinese Youths and Democratic Belonging — The Politics of Pragmatism and Fairness .

items.title: Bajau Sama oral art maestro named National Living Heritage Figure
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Bajau Sama's traditional oral art has earned national recognition, with its leading practitioner, Masruh Siadik, named a National Living Heritage Figure (WAKOH) 2026. Masruh was recognised in the Language and Literature Arts category for his contributions to preserving, developing and promoting Isun-Isun, a traditional art form practised by the Bajau Sama and Iranun communities in Kota Belud. Since the National Heritage Act 2005 (Act 645) came into force, 27 cultural practitioners from various ethnic, cultural and religious backgrounds have been recognised as National Living Heritage Figures.

items.title: Raja Puan Muda of Kedah meets families of Malaysians missing in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians missing in the Nepal floods have sought clarification on delayed financial assistance and other benefits during an audience with the Raja Puan Muda of Kedah, Che Puan Muda Zaheeda Mohamad Ariff. Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) coordinator and spokesperson Dr R. Manivannan said the families also sought updates on the disbursement of benefits from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso). However, Manivannan said only the RM3,000 assistance had reached the 28 affected families so far, while pension payments and other benefits remained outstanding.

items.title: Dutch Lady buys 35pct stake in Jemaluang Dairy from Kulim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd has agreed to buy a 35 per cent stake in Johor-based integrated dairy business Jemaluang Dairy Valley Sdn Bhd from Kulim (Malaysia) Bhd. Upon completion, Dutch Lady Malaysia will join Kulim, a wholly owned subsidiary of Johor Corporation (JCorp), and A2 Fresh Holdings Sdn Bhd (A2F), a subsidiary of Rhone Ma Holdings Bhd, as shareholders in Jemaluang Dairy. Dutch Lady Malaysia said the investment will strengthen its presence in the domestic fresh milk segment as the country seeks to expand local dairy production and improve food security.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine hold first peace talks for nine months, gaps have narrowed
items.summary: ABU DHABI: Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first US-brokered talks since February, after President Donald Trump suggested last week that a broad deal was possible on ending the war in Ukraine and guaranteeing security in Europe. Ukraine's chief delegate, Rustem Umerov, said in his opening remarks that Kyiv was focused on achieving security guarantees and a lasting peace. [[nid:1574838]] Russian delegation chief Vladimir Medinsky said Moscow hoped for progress towards peace in the interest of the peoples of both countries.

items.title: Malaysian sukuk remains most liquid: Fitch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian ringgit-denominated sukuk have maintained liquidity above pre-Iran conflict levels, outperforming the broader global sukuk market amid continued geopolitical uncertainty, according to Fitch Ratings. "Malaysian ringgit sukuk remained the most liquid, continuing to trade above pre-conflict liquidity levels. "The liquidity score of euro-denominated sukuk rose to about 81.

items.title: Anwar shares light-hearted moment with Trevor Noah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today received a visit from South African comedian Trevor Noah ahead of his show tonight. Anwar said they discussed politics, humour and various other topics during a meeting filled with laughter. he said.

items.title: Lianson adds DP2 heavy-lift vessel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lianson Fleet Group Bhd (LFG) has unveiled the LFG Hercules, the first Malaysian-flagged dynamic positioning class 2 (DP2) offshore heavy-lift vessel, following its acquisition in October. With a lifting capacity of up to 4,000 metric tonnes, the vessel is designed to support large-scale offshore operations, including decommissioning, heavy-lift installation and construction, as well as renewable energy infrastructure projects. He said LFG Hercules will broaden the group's service offerings and provide opportunities in offshore decommissioning, heavy-lift work and offshore renewable energy infrastructure.

items.title: KPJ tops Asean healthcare brand strength, 2nd in value at US$305mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KPJ Healthcare Bhd has emerged as Asean's strongest healthcare facilities brand, according to the Brand Finance Asean 500 2026 report, with a Brand Strength Index score of 86.8 out of 100. The healthcare group also ranked second among Asean's most valuable healthcare facilities brands, after its brand value rose 45 per cent to US$305 million from US$211 million in 2025. KPJ is expanding its healthcare network through its KPJ Health System, which combines clinical practice, education, and research and innovation.

items.title: Data centre operators must bear electricity, infrastructure costs, says Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: New data centre applications must take into account electricity supply availability and the ability of states to meet water demand, says Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. The investment, trade and industry minister said the growth of data centres must also be managed responsibly, with operators bearing the cost of electricity supply and necessary infrastructure. "The cost of electricity supply and the necessary infrastructure must be borne by operators rather than passed on to the public or existing businesses.

items.title: AmBank offers six-month flood relief
items.summary: The assistance is also available to customers in other areas designated as flood disaster zones by the National Disaster Management Agency. AmBank Group chief executive officer Jamie Ling said the assistance was intended to ease the financial burden on affected customers as they focus on recovery. Affected customers can apply for the assistance and get more details through AmBank's flood relief programme.

items.title: 'Burning': Life under the world's dirtiest skies
items.summary: ON the outskirts of India's capital, a short motorbike ride through the urban area with the world's worst air pollution leaves salesman Kanwar Singh coated in toxic dust. "It enters my throat and lungs," the 55-year-old cigarette seller told AFP, running his hands over his clothes to show the fine dust. During winter pollution peaks, when colder air traps pollutants close to the ground, PM2.5 readings can exceed 800 micrograms per cubic metre – more than 50 times the WHO's 24-hour guideline.

items.title: Anthony Loke officially resigns as transport minister following court decision on Najib
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook has resigned as transport minister with immediate effect following the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision allowing former prime minister Najib Tun Razak to serve his sentence under house arrest, according to a statement issued today. He expressed his appreciation to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim for the trust and mandate given to him to serve in the Cabinet since December 2022. Loke also thanked the senior management and staff of the Ministry of Transport for their commitment and cooperation throughout his tenure at the ministry.

items.title: Najib to serve remaining jail term at home after High Court issues new warrant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The High Court has directed the Court Registrar to issue a new order that would finally allow Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Abdul Razak to serve the remaining sentence of his first corruption conviction at home. High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin issued the new warrant of release after hearing submissions by both Najib’s lawyers and the Deputy Public Prosecutors this afternoon. Judge Aslam said the new order simply cancels the November 6 order and replaced with one that allows Najib to serve the remaining sentence from the said conviction at home.

items.title: Kuala Kangsar Sessions Court orders mental health assessment for accused in rape, attempted murder case
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Nov 10 — The Sessions Court here today ordered a man who pleaded guilty to attempting to murder and raping a woman to undergo a psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Tanjung Rambutan. Judge Nuur Hafiedzah Md Daud issued the order against Marwan Mohd Nor, 38, under Section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code after observing the accused’s demeanour when he pleaded guilty to both charges. Earlier, Marwan pleaded guilty to both charges and appealed to the court to impose the maximum sentence for the rape charge.

items.title: ITU PP-26: Appointment of Malaysian representative as Committee 5 chair reflects international confidence
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 10 — Malaysia’s appointment as chair of Committee 5 at the 2026 International Telecommunication Union Plenipotentiary Conference (ITU PP-26) reflects the international community’s confidence in the country’s ability to play a neutral role in balancing the interests of various parties. Committee 5 chair Eneng Faridah Iskandar said the appointment was not merely a personal recognition but a major achievement for Malaysia, according to a report published by Bernama. Explaining Committee 5’s role, Eneng Faridah said the substantive committee was responsible for examining various policy and legal issues within the ITU framework.

items.title: Not cutting-edge: Men armed with scissors in Tuaran gang robbery to be sentenced on Nov 20
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 10 — Three men who pleaded guilty to a charge of gang robbery armed with scissors will know their fate on November 20. Sessions Court Judge Monica Linsua adjourned the sentencing of the men, aged 29, 26, and 35 respectively, under Section 395 of the Penal Code, which is punishable under Section 397 of the same Code, at the request of the prosecution. The men had admitted robbing another two men of their cash and two mobile phones by the roadside of Jalan Berungis in Tuaran at 12.50am on Oct 26.

items.title: MWC Doha: Fahmi shares Malaysia’s 5G network progress, 90pc coverage achieved ahead of schedule
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 10 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil shared Malaysia’s progress in expanding its 5G network at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026, with the country’s second 5G network achieving 90 per cent coverage last October, nine months ahead of schedule. Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela) since 2020. However, Fahmi stressed that Malaysia’s digital infrastructure development was not solely focused on expanding network coverage, but also on service quality, subscription affordability and network resilience.

items.title: Najib in court as lawyers, AGC discuss fresh house arrest order
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Datuk Seri Najib Razak is present as the High Court hears the application for a new order to allow the former prime minister to serve his first jail sentence at home. Najib, in a light blue baju melayu top with sleeves rolled up, was present at the hearing alongside his daughter Najwa, who was in a blue floral baju kurung. The High Court is expected to issue a new warrant to release Najib from Kajang Prison this afternoon itself.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan takes politics to coffee shops with Gen Z-focused ‘Kopilih Harapan’ initiative
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is adopting a new approach to engage young people, particularly Generation Z, through its ‘Kopilih Harapan’ programme, which provides an informal platform for political leaders and members of the public to discuss current issues and aspirations. PH Election Department (JPPH) Media Unit head Jonathan Vela said the programme aims to foster more open and inclusive two-way communication, moving away from conventional political ceramah. He said the coffee shop-themed initiative allows young people to raise questions, share their views and seek clarification directly from PH leaders and candidates.

items.title: Skilled workforce crucial to unlocking Malaysia’s high-tech investment potential, says minister
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 10 — Developing a highly skilled workforce must remain a priority for Malaysia to fully capitalise on opportunities arising from digital transformation and the rapid growth of high-tech industries. Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said that while Malaysia continues to attract billions of ringgit in high-tech sector investments, the country’s success ultimately depends on its local workforce’s ability to master and harness emerging technologies. Chang said industry investments in human capital development also reinforced the principle that Malaysia’s greatest asset was its people, ensuring national innovation policies translated into tangible economic outcomes.

items.title: Police deployed outside Najib’s residence amid home detention rumours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Police maintained a presence outside former prime minister Najib Razak's residence today as speculation grew over his possible return home under a reported house arrest arrangement. According to China Press, several police vehicles and personnel were seen stationed near the property in Jalan Langgak Duta throughout the day. Media personnel and members of the public also gathered outside the residence following widespread rumours that Najib could be transferred from prison to serve the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: Pertak river water surge: Search for three missing victims widened to Sungai Selangor dam
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR, Nov 10 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for three people still missing following a water surge incident at Lata Jebus, near the Sungai Pertak waterfall in Kampung Pertak here, has been extended to the Sungai Selangor Dam, about three kilometres from the scene. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said search efforts were concentrated along Sungai Luit, from Lata Jebus towards the dam. Ashrul Riezal said the first victim, identified as V. Vijayan, 36, was found near the Pertak Bridge at 1.30am today, about 2.7 kilometres from where he was swept away.

items.title: Vehicle believed to be carrying Najib seen leaving Kajang Prison amid court proceedings over house arrest order
items.summary: KAJANG, Nov 10 — A grey sport utility vehicle (SUV) believed to be carrying former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was seen leaving the Kajang Prison Complex at about 2.40pm today, escorted by several prison security vehicles. The departure came as Najib’s lawyers were scheduled to attend a court mention over the dispute surrounding an order allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest. The matter was listed before High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Criminal Court 5 at 2.30pm today.

items.title: Johor pawn shop heist: Seven arrested, former manager suspected of masterminding RM28.4m theft, says police chief
items.summary: Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspect allegedly entered the premises through the front entrance and exited through the back with the items and cash at 11.42am. Acting on information, he said police arrested seven individuals, consisting of five men and two women. Following the arrests, Ab Rahaman said police seized 2,891 pieces of jewellery, RM27,371 in cash, two pawn receipts, two sets of keys, two sling bags and a mobile phone.

items.title: Health inflation in Malaysia more than doubles to 3pc in 2025, says Stats Dept
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 10 — Health Inflation increased 3.0 per cent in 2025 as compared to 1.3 per cent in 2024, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). It said the increase was driven by the Health Services category, which recorded a significant rise of 4.4 per cent as compared to 0.9 per cent in 2024, which contributed by the Insurance connected with health expenditure class that increased by 9.1 per cent in 2025 (2024: 0.0%). The Medicine category represents the largest weight, accounting for 38.9 per cent in Health Price Index (HPI), recorded an increase of 2.8 per cent in 2025, compared with 2.2 per cent in the previous year.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues storm warning for parts of Selangor, Johor, KL and six other states until 5pm today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in parts of 10 states and Kuala Lumpur until 5pm today, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said. In a warning issued at 12.45pm, the department said the affected areas include the whole of Perlis, as well as Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap and Pokok Sena in Kedah. The warning also covers Kuala Lumpur, Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan, and Pontian, Johor Baru, Kulai and Mersing in Johor.

items.title: ITU PP-26: Malaysia developing national plan for post-quantum cryptography, says Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 10 — Malaysia is developing a national plan to transition its critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography, as part of efforts to strengthen cybersecurity and prepare the country for emerging threats posed by quantum computing. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had instructed the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to engage with the National Security Council (MKN), National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) and telecommunications operators to establish a shared research and development (R&D) testbed. “Malaysia is developing a national plan to move critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography.

items.title: Police probe boy’s fall after clinging to moving vehicle near Nilai toll plaza
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 10 — Police are investigating an incident involving a boy who fell onto the road after clinging to the rear door of a moving vehicle, as seen in a video that went viral on social media, believed to have occurred near the Nilai toll plaza here. Nilai police chief Supt Johari Yahya said police received a report on the circulation of the one-minute video at 11.02pm yesterday. Johari said police were now working to verify the information, including recording a statement from the dashboard camera owner and tracing the boy and his family members to assist in the investigation.

items.title: Court to hear AGC application for fresh order to facilitate Najib's house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The High Court in Kuala Lumpur is expected to have a hearing this afternoon the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) application to correct a court order or issue a fresh court order to enable former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest. When contacted today, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed to Malay Mail t hat there would be a court hearing this afternoon for the AGC’s “Rectification Application”. Earlier today, Dusuki confirmed to Malay Mail that the AGC had asked the courts to issue a new court order for the house arrest.

items.title: Penang includes mitigation plans at flood hotspots under 2040 structure plan
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — Penang’s draft Structure Plan 2040 includes proposals to upgrade flood hotspots and install pumps in certain areas, state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said today. He said the proposed measures included the installation of flood mitigation infrastructure at selected locations. He also said state exco Zairil Khir Johari has several flood mitigation projects in his portfolio to resolve flooding in hotspots in the state.

items.title: Residents of four affected homes in Paya Terubong still not allowed to return home as DOSH awaits mitigation plan
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — The residents of four houses affected by the fatal landslide in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, have yet to be allowed to return home, state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said today. He said the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is still waiting for the developer’s civil engineer, Aptitute Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, to submit full documentations and a formal application to carry out mitigation and repair works at the collapsed slope. He said DOSH had requested a landslide report from the developer’s geotechnical engineer, WYA Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, and the company had submitted the report on November 5.

items.title: AG: Courts asked to issue new house arrest order for Najib
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Attorney-General’s Chambers has asked the courts to issue a new order for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest in line with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s September pardon, the attorney general said today. Yesterday, local daily Berita Harian reported Dusuki as saying the High Court in Kuala Lumpur's Order of Discharge for Najib contained obvious errors or defects. On November 6, Umno paid the RM50 million fine on Najib's behalf, which resulted in the High Court in Kuala Lumpur issuing an Order of Discharge to enable Najib's house arrest to take place.

items.title: Floods, storm and landslide leave 422 evacuees at relief centres in Perak, Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — A total of 422 evacuees from 119 families remain at temporary relief centres (PPS) in Perak and Selangor as of this morning. In Perak, the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat said the number of flood evacuees had dropped to 410 people from 114 families, compared with 419 people from 124 families last night. It said all evacuees were currently housed at three PPS in two districts.

items.title: DAP committed to nation-building regardless of govt or opposition role, says veep Teo Nie Ching
items.summary: KULAI, Nov 10 — The DAP wants to continue playing its role as a nation-building party, regardless of whether it is in government or the opposition, by championing transparent, fair and sustainable policies, said its vice-president Teo Nie Ching. Teo, who is also deputy communications minister, said the principle formed the basis of DAP’s struggle to ensure Malaysia continued to develop as a nation with a sustainable governance system, while prioritising the interests and welfare of the people. Commenting on DAP’s participation in the Madani Government, Teo said its position provided the party with an opportunity to translate its principles into policies and action through direct involvement in the country’s administration.
